contentHtml:
The most popular luxury TV unit designs for the hall in 2026 are fluted veneer walls, Italian marble or stone-look panels, floating consoles with hidden storage, and backlit walls with profile lighting. A custom luxury TV wall in a Gurgaon home typically costs ₹1–4 lakh, depending on size and finish.

The TV wall is usually the first thing you see when you walk into a living room. In a premium Gurgaon apartment or villa, it does more than hold a screen: it hides wires and the set-top box, stores clutter, and becomes the main design feature of the room. Here are 10 ideas, what each costs, and how to choose. For the rest of the room, see our luxury living room designs for 3BHK and 4BHK flats.

10 luxury TV unit designs for your hall

Fluted veneer, marble or stone-look panels, floating consoles and backlit walls lead luxury TV unit design in 2026. These are the 10 ideas we see working best in Gurgaon homes:

1. Full-height fluted veneer wall

Vertical wood flutes in walnut, smoked oak or teak veneer, running floor to ceiling behind the TV. Mount the TV a few centimetres proud of the wall so the flutes frame it. This is the most requested luxury TV wall in 2026.

2. Italian marble or stone-look feature wall

A book-matched Statuario or onyx-look slab behind the TV makes an instant statement. Large-format porcelain slabs give the same look at a lower cost and are lighter on the wall.

3. Floating console with hidden storage

A wall-hung console 12–15 inches off the floor, with push-to-open drawers for the set-top box, router and remotes. The open floor below makes the room feel bigger and is easier to clean.

4. Backlit TV wall with profile lighting

Warm 2700K–3000K LED strips behind the panel or along the console create a soft glow and reduce eye strain when watching in the evening. Use a separate switch or dimmer.

5. Veneer and PU combination

Pair a natural wood veneer panel with matt PU-finished storage below. It looks warm and expensive, and is one of the most popular premium finishes for TV units.

6. TV wall with display niches

Open niches on one or both sides, lit from above, for art, books or collectibles. Keep the niches deep enough (about 10–12 inches) for real objects, not just decoration.

7. Concealed TV wall with sliding panels

Sliding fluted or lacquered panels hide the TV completely when it is off, so the living room reads as a calm, formal space for guests.

8. Combined TV and study or bar unit

In larger 4BHK and villa halls, extend the TV wall into a bar counter or a small work desk on one side. One continuous unit looks better than several separate pieces.

9. Minimal handleless TV unit

Flat, handleless shutters in a single colour (taupe, charcoal or ivory) with no visible hardware. This modern TV unit design suits contemporary homes and shows off a large screen.

10. TV wall with integrated mandir (where space is tight)

In compact 2BHK and 3BHK flats, some families combine the TV wall with a small mandir unit on one side, separated by a panel or jaali. Keep the mandir slightly raised and give it its own lighting so the two uses stay distinct.

How much does a luxury TV unit design cost in Gurgaon?

A custom luxury TV wall in a Gurgaon home typically costs ₹1–4 lakh, depending on size and finish. These are the indicative rates for units and wall panels:

Example: a 10 × 9 ft luxury TV wall

ItemCalculationCost

Profile lighting6 m × ₹2,000₹12,000
Side display nicheLump sum₹15,000 – ₹25,000
Total≈ ₹1.25 – 1.35 lakh

Swap the veneer panel for book-matched Italian marble, or extend the unit into a bar, and the same wall can cost ₹3–4 lakh or more.

How do you choose the right TV unit design?

Start with viewing distance and wiring, then choose finishes that suit Gurgaon's climate and the rest of the room:

  • Measure the viewing distance: for a 65-inch TV, sit roughly 8–10 ft away. The TV centre should be near eye level when seated, about 42–48 inches from the floor.
  • Plan wiring before carpentry: get concealed conduits for HDMI, power and the set-top box, plus a spare pipe for future cables. Fixing this after the panel goes up means breaking it. If you are adding automation, plan it with our smart home wiring guide.
  • Choose finishes for Gurgaon's climate: use BWP plywood or HDHMR for the carcass. Hot, dry summers and humid monsoons can warp cheap MDF and lift edge banding.
  • Ventilate the electronics: leave gaps or perforations behind closed shutters so the set-top box, router and amplifier do not overheat.
  • Match the rest of the room: pick the TV wall finish together with the flooring, sofa and ceiling, not on its own.

faqs.question: What is the latest luxury TV unit design for the hall in 2026?
faqs.answer: Full-height fluted veneer walls, Italian marble or stone-look panels, floating consoles and backlit walls with warm LED profile lighting are the most popular luxury TV unit designs in 2026.

faqs.question: How much does a luxury TV unit cost in Gurgaon?
faqs.answer: A custom luxury TV wall in Gurgaon typically costs ₹1–4 lakh. A 10 × 9 ft wall with a veneer fluted panel, floating console and profile lighting costs about ₹1.25–1.35 lakh. Marble cladding or a combined bar unit costs more.

faqs.question: Which material is best for a TV unit?
faqs.answer: BWP plywood or HDHMR for the structure, with laminate for durability on a budget, or veneer with matt PU for a premium wood look. Avoid plain MDF for the carcass in Gurgaon's humid monsoon months.

faqs.question: At what height should a TV be mounted in the living room?
faqs.answer: The centre of the screen should be close to seated eye level, usually about 42–48 inches from the floor, depending on your sofa height.

faqs.question: Is a wall-mounted or floor-standing TV unit better?
faqs.answer: A wall-mounted, floating unit looks lighter, makes the room feel bigger and is easier to clean under. A floor-standing unit gives more storage and suits larger halls with heavy audio equipment.
